reason: E1 shows synthesis of sub-nanometer HEA clusters on CeO2 nanorods and in situ XAFS evidence of reversible structural changes under NO/H2 cycling, supporting premises 1, 2, and 5. However, E1 does not directly demonstrate the sacrificial oxidation/reduction mechanism (premises 3 and 4) or confirm that the single-phase solid solution is fully restored after reduction. E2 describes a self-regenerative mechanism in a different high-entropy oxide system, not metallic HEA clusters on CeO2, so it provides only indirect conceptual support.
premises: Sub-nanometer HEA clusters can be synthesized on CeO2 nanorods as uniform solid solutions
Reversible oxidation–reduction cycling of HEA clusters on CeO2 is possible
The high-entropy composition enables sacrificial oxidation without permanent phase separation
Subsequent reduction restores the metallic single-phase solid solution
This self-healing mechanism preserves structural integrity under catalytic redox cycling
